The Rust core dialed the station over QUIC and holds the session while this app runs. Everything here is the real state of that connection — the webview never touches the network.

Chat

rooms on the mesh
No rooms yet
Chat over rooms lands on top of the live mesh link — join and talk to whoever is on the mesh. This tab will show your joined rooms and their conversations.

Teams

who is working on what
The team board is next
Open lanes, open handoffs, recent results, help broadcasts and the roster — derived in the Rust core from the mesh's own message kinds, per the team-coordination exploration.

Services

the DHT procedure catalog
The catalog is next
Every capability advertised on the mesh, discoverable from the station's DHT — filterable and callable right here.

Realms

membership and trust domains
Realm membership is next
Your memberships, org identity and trust tier — joining happens through the same flow the terminal client uses.

Local Applications

admin UIs on your LAN

Hecate services running on your edge boxes expose plain-HTTP admin UIs to the LAN. Clicking a card embeds its UI right here (the sidebar stays); the system browser is one click away. Add and remove cards below — they persist to the config file.

Mesh Applications

UIs served through the mesh

Applications hosted elsewhere on the mesh, named by MRI. Add the ones you know; their resolution through the mesh lands with the DHT-discovery slice — the card shows the MRI until then.
